Hebronites
HEB-run-ytes
n. (the Levitical clan descended from Hebron, son of Kohath)
Hebrew Chevroni (H2276), from Chevron, a son of Kohath; not to be confused with the city of the same name in Judah.

Biblical Definition

The Hebronites are one of the four Levitical clans descended from Kohath, named for their ancestor Hebron son of Kohath — a man wholly distinct from the city of the same name in Judah. The census of the Kohathites lists them plainly: “of Kohath was the family of the Amramites, and the family of the Izeharites, and the family of the Hebronites, and the family of the Uzzielites: these are the families of the Kohathites” (Numbers 3:27), a listing repeated in the wilderness census a generation later (Numbers 26:58). By David’s day the clan had grown into a substantial force in the kingdom’s administration: “of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brethren, men of valour, a thousand and seven hundred, were officers among them of Israel on this side Jordan westward in all the business of the LORD, and in the service of the king” (1 Chronicles 26:30), with a further company under Jerijah stationed east of Jordan (1 Chronicles 26:31–32) — Levites serving not only at the altar but in civil administration under a king who understood that even the kingdom’s business belonged, in the end, to the LORD. The clan’s own genealogy within Hebron’s house is further detailed: “of the sons of Hebron; Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth” (1 Chronicles 23:19).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no entry for Hebronites; they are one of the four Levitical clans of Kohath, named for their ancestor Hebron, and served both at the altar and in David's civil administration.

expand to see more

HEBRONITES, n. A Levitical family descended from Hebron, son of Kohath, prominent in David's administration.

LEVITE, n. A member of the tribe of Levi, set apart for the service of the tabernacle and temple.

KOHATHITES, n. One of the three great Levitical divisions, descended from Kohath, charged with the sanctuary's holiest furniture.

OFFICER, n. One who holds a post of authority or trust in the administration of civil or ecclesiastical affairs.

VALOUR, n. Strength of mind in regard to danger; personal bravery; boldness in facing danger.

Key Scripture

Numbers 3:27 — "And of Kohath was the family of the Amramites, and the family of the Izeharites, and the family of the Hebronites, and the family of the Uzzielites: these are the families of the Kohathites."

Numbers 26:58 — "These are the families of the Levites: the family of the Libnites, the family of the Hebronites, the family of the Mahlites, the family of the Mushites, the family of the Korathites. And Kohath begat Amram."

1 Chronicles 26:30 — "And of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brethren, men of valour, a thousand and seven hundred, were officers among them of Israel on this side Jordan westward in all the business of the LORD, and in the service of the king."

1 Chronicles 23:19 — "Of the sons of Hebron; Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth."

Modern Corruption

The consistent, unglamorous census-list use of this clan name across Numbers and Chronicles, centuries apart, is the pattern of careful genealogical record-keeping, not late literary schematizing.

expand to see more

Source-critical theories that assign the priestly census material in Numbers to a late, artificial, post-exilic construction still have to account for the Chronicler's independent and internally consistent use of the same clan structure centuries afterward, right down to naming a fourth-generation officer roster. A late inventor working from imagination, not archive, does not typically reproduce a rival book's minor administrative clan names this precisely.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the LORD's service under David extended past the altar into the ordinary work of the kingdom — men set apart from birth for sacred duty were also entrusted with civil administration, a pattern that refuses any hard sacred-secular divide and insists that all of life, rightly ordered under the LORD's law, is service to Him (Colossians 3:23–24).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Chevroni (H2276), from Chevron (H2275); Qehathi (H6956), Kohathite; chayil (H2428), valour, strength; abodah (H5656), service, work.

expand to see more

Hebrew Chevroni (H2276) — Hebronite, from the ancestor Hebron son of Kohath.

Hebrew Qehathi (H6956) — Kohathite; the larger Levitical division the Hebronites belong to.

Hebrew chayil (H2428) — valour, strength, ability; the Chronicler's description of Hashabiah's men.

Hebrew abodah (H5656) — service, work; the word covering both sanctuary duty and the king's business.

Hebrew paqid (H6496), related to peqidah (H6486) — officer, overseer; the office David gave this clan.

Usage

"“The family of the Hebronites, and the family of the Uzzielites” — their place among the Kohathite clans."

"“Men of valour... officers... in all the business of the LORD, and in the service of the king” — their role under David."

"“Of the sons of Hebron; Jeriah the first” — the clan's own internal genealogy."
